Thanks Emma — looping in Dylan (sales ops) and Olga (finance) to provide the official treatment and next steps. Quick summary from product/legal side:

- For recurring Dedicated/Hosted fees (software, managed service, support) we treat these as supplies of services. For B2B cross-border within the EU/UK we typically apply the reverse-charge mechanism provided the buyer gives a valid VAT registration number and is a business in the relevant jurisdiction.
- The VAT Margin Scheme is specifically for second‑hand goods/persons dealing in used goods and only applies to physical goods where the seller is using the margin scheme in their VAT accounting — it does not apply to software/subscription services.

That said, we need finance to confirm the one hardware line. Olga, can you confirm whether Redwood sold used hardware in this transaction and whether we typically account for such disposals under the margin scheme? If not, what remediation do you recommend (credit + reissue vs annotation)?

Emma — could you also share the VAT registration number for BrightPay and a short note confirming AP are a taxable business? That will let us confirm reverse-charge for the service lines quickly.

Happy to run a 20-min call if that speeds things up.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: VAT treatment query on invoice #4512 — margin scheme or reverse-charge?

Hi all — tagging in from Finance. Short answers up front:

- Margin scheme: We do not apply the VAT margin scheme as a standard for disposals unless the transaction is a) a sale of second‑hand goods and b) the seller (Redwood) is explicitly operating a margin scheme accounting method for that line. Our bookkeeping does not currently use the margin scheme for routine hardware disposals.

- Reverse-charge: For B2B cross-border services (including hosted services and SaaS) between EU businesses and UK businesses, reverse-charge is the normal treatment when the buyer provides a valid VAT ID and confirms business status. That means the invoice should be annotated with the reverse-charge reference ("VAT reverse charge — customer to account for VAT") and our VAT ID included.

Recommended remediation options for invoice #4512 (choose one):
1) Issue a credit note for #4512 and reissue a corrected invoice that: marks service lines as reverse-charge (if BrightPay provides VAT ID) and separates the hardware line for separate evaluation.
2) If BrightPay confirms the hardware line is a resale of used goods and they want margin-scheme treatment, provide: (i) evidence of the original purchase price for the used chassis and (ii) confirmation you are comfortable with our issuing a margin-scheme invoice. Finance will then determine if a retrospective margin treatment is permissible.
3) If BrightPay prefers not to delay payment, we can add an invoice note for internal AP that the service lines are reverse-charge pending VAT ID verification; we’d still reissue a corrected invoice after verification (this is not ideal for auditors).

Please note: if we reissue and annotate reverse-charge that will not alter the amount you owe — it only changes VAT accounting/presentation. If you need a credit to reflect a different VAT calculation we’ll have to reissue with updated totals.

Next steps: Emma, please send the BrightPay VAT Registration Number and a scan of the AP sign-off. Also confirm whether the surplus chassis should be treated as a hardware resale candidate under margin-scheme rules and attach any supporting purchase docs. I’ll prepare a draft credit + replacement invoice once we have the VAT ID.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Billing Lead — Redwood Inference
